notes: The scribe's name is garbled in the catalogue: 'litaṃ (12\u2 2 1 dha 4ī) rmmaṇāḥ'. 'litaṃ' is probably 'li[khi]taṃ' and 'rmmaṇāḥ' is the end of '-śarmaṇā', an instrumental with a stray visarga. So the scribe was a brahmin whose name contains something like 'dha' and 'ī'. The name itself cannot be recovered. 'dinagatā 13' may mean day 13 of a solar month, which would make month 7 = Tulā. It may instead mean 13 ghaṭikās elapsed. Month numbering is therefore ambiguous. ŚS 1629 = 1707 CE. This matches the catalogue field, but the date has not been checked against an ephemeris. The verses after the date ('tailād rakṣe…', 'bhagnapṛṣṭhakaṭīgrīvā…', 'rāma rāmeti…') are stock scribal verses. They name no persons.
